name: table-cell-attributes
body:
A cell's content carries, beyond inline Markdown, a line break and attribute groups. `{br}` is a line break anywhere in a cell and renders as `
` in the cell's HTML. An attribute group `{…}` is recognised in a cell's content outside an inline code span and outside a link's text and destination — the convention is at the cell's end — and sets one or more declared cell attributes: `{highlight:green}` sets `highlight` to `green`; `{bold}` sets the boolean `bold` to true (`{bold}` is `{bold:true}`); a group may set several attributes, as `{highlight:green, bold}` does. A backslash-escaped brace (`\{`) is a literal brace, not a group. Inside an inline code span a brace is literal cell-content text: a code span such as `` `{bold}` `` renders the text `{bold}` and declares no attribute, exactly as `\|` is a literal pipe inside a code span (table-syntax). Inside a link the braces of both its text and its destination (`[text](destination)`) are literal as well: a `{…}` there is part of the link's text or URL and declares no attribute, so a group that decorates a linked cell sits outside the link, for example after it at the cell's end. `br` is reserved and is never a declarable cell attribute. Short-hand names resolve by mutex: a bare name that is the variant of exactly one declared enum cell attribute sets that attribute to that variant, so `{green}` sets `highlight:green` when `green` is a variant of the one declared `highlight` enum; a cell holds at most one value per attribute by construction. A bare name that is both a declared boolean attribute and an enum variant, or a variant of more than one declared enum attribute, is a template load error naming the ambiguous name — a templates error path-qualified to the offending `template.yaml`. A boolean attribute's `{name:true}`/`{name:false}` and an enum attribute's `{name:variant}` are always accepted; a value that is not of the attribute's declared type is a validation error naming the attribute and the value. A cell attribute is declared in the template's `body.tables.cell_attributes` list with the usual field descriptors (`name`, `type`, and an enum's `variants`), and is type-checked. An attribute a cell uses that its enclosing template does not declare is an error with a closest-match suggestion, for example `unknown cell attribute "hilight": did you mean "highlight"?`. Attributes apply to header cells exactly as to body cells. AC: `{br}` renders a `
` in a cell; `{highlight:green}` sets the enum attribute; `{bold}` equals `{bold:true}`; `{highlight:green, bold}` sets both; `\{` is a literal brace; a `{…}` inside an inline code span is literal text that declares no attribute (a cell `` `{bold}` `` renders `{bold}` and sets no attribute); a `{…}` inside a link's text or destination is literal too (a group for a linked cell sits at the cell's end, after the link); `{green}` resolves to the sole matching enum variant; a bare name that is both a declared boolean and an enum variant, or a variant of two enums, is a template load error; an unknown attribute is an error with the closest-match suggestion over the declared attributes; a wrong-typed value is a validation error; `br` declared as a cell attribute is a templates error; a header cell's attribute is exposed exactly like a body cell's.
